concepts.heading: The Performance Script
concepts.alt: A guide standing on a stage under a spotlight holding a scorecard, looking nervous
concepts.plain: Many of us learned to treat sex like a show we have to get right.

concepts.heading: What Is Pleasure, Really?
concepts.alt: A guide savouring a warm cup with her eyes closed, a small heart above
concepts.plain: Pleasure is anything that feels good, in your body, your feelings or your connection.

concepts.heading: The Pleasure Spectrum
concepts.alt: A guide holding a long colour bar that fades from soft pink to deep purple
concepts.plain: Pleasure can be soft or strong. Every level counts.

concepts.heading: Why Performance Pressure Kills Pleasure
concepts.alt: A guide carrying a heavy stopwatch-shaped weight on his shoulders
concepts.plain: Pressure to perform hits the brakes and shuts pleasure down.

concepts.heading: Normalizing Diverse Pleasure Preferences
concepts.plain: People like very different things. All of it deserves respect.

checks.prompt: How does the lesson define pleasure?
checks.explanation: Any experience that feels good. Pleasure is any experience that feels good — physically, emotionally, or relationally.

checks.prompt: Performance pressure switches on which part of the dual control model?
checks.explanation: The brakes. Performance pressure activates the sexual inhibition system — the brakes in the dual control model.

e819f05f-bb0a-4872-acba-900e21839ae2.takeaway: Sex is not a performance. Pleasure is whatever truly feels good to you.

concepts.heading: Know Yourself First
concepts.alt: A guide looking curiously into a heart-shaped hand mirror
concepts.plain: Getting to know what you enjoy is the first step.

concepts.heading: Creating Your Pleasure Map
concepts.alt: A guide drawing a treasure map dotted with hearts and stars
concepts.plain: A pleasure map is your own list of what feels good, where and how. It keeps changing.

concepts.heading: Solo Exploration as Valid Sexuality
concepts.plain: Exploring on your own is real, complete sexuality. It is not second best.

concepts.heading: Tools and Aids
concepts.alt: A guide holding an open toolbox with a feather, a bottle and a ribbon inside
concepts.plain: Toys and lube are helpful tools. Using them does not mean something is lacking.

concepts.heading: Erotic Blueprints
concepts.alt: A guide holding five coloured cards fanned out, each with a different simple icon
concepts.plain: People tend to have a "type" of touch or mood that works best for them.

concepts.heading: Sharing Your Map
concepts.alt: She hands him a rolled-up map tied with a ribbon
concepts.plain: Telling a partner what you like is a gift, not a demand.

checks.prompt: How does the lesson describe solo exploration?
options: A complete, valid experience in its own right
checks.explanation: A complete, valid experience in its own right. Solo sexual exploration is not a substitute for partnered sex — it's a complete, valid sexual experience in its own right.

checks.prompt: Sharing your pleasure map with a partner is described as an act of…
checks.explanation: Generosity and trust. Once you know your pleasure map, sharing it with partners becomes an act of generosity and trust.

5f4c3ba8-078e-42e3-ad7c-47bc41807b99.takeaway: Learn what you enjoy, then share it with your partners.

concepts.heading: What Is Sensate Focus?
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting facing each other, gently touching fingertips
concepts.plain: Sensate focus is a slow touching exercise with no goal except noticing.

concepts.heading: The Progressive Stages
concepts.alt: A guide climbing three wide steps, each glowing a little brighter
concepts.plain: It moves in stages, starting with touch away from private areas.

concepts.heading: Why Removing Goals Works
concepts.alt: A guide tossing a finish flag over his shoulder, relaxed and smiling
concepts.plain: When there is nothing to achieve, pressure drops and feeling comes back.

concepts.heading: Adapting Sensate Focus
concepts.plain: You can adjust it for any body, any partner and any relationship.

concepts.heading: Building Presence
concepts.alt: A guide sitting peacefully with open hands, a paused hourglass beside her
concepts.plain: The real prize is being fully present with yourself and your partner.

checks.explanation: A structured touching exercise. Sensate focus is a structured touching exercise originally developed by sex researchers William Masters and Virginia Johnson in the 1960s as a therapeutic technique for couples experiencing sexual difficulties.

checks.prompt: Sensate focus works partly by removing what?
checks.explanation: Sexual goals. This may sound counterintuitive: how does removing sexual goals improve sexual experiences?

e497a740-abfc-485f-bb17-02e31a911af3.takeaway: Slow touch with no goal takes the pressure off and brings feeling back.

concepts.heading: Why Talking About Pleasure Is Hard
concepts.alt: A guide with a zip over his mouth and a speech bubble full of tangled scribble
concepts.plain: Most people find it hard to say what feels good. Shame and fear get in the way.

concepts.heading: Communication Tools That Work
concepts.alt: A guide holding a speech bubble that contains a heart and a thumbs up
concepts.plain: Simple starters help, like "I like when..." and "Could we try...".

concepts.heading: Giving and Receiving Feedback
concepts.alt: She gives him a small gift box while he listens with a smile
concepts.plain: Give feedback kindly and clearly. Take feedback without getting defensive.

concepts.heading: The Ongoing Conversation
concepts.plain: What you like changes over time, so keep talking about it.

concepts.heading: Pleasure Communication in ENM
concepts.alt: Three guides sitting together, each with a differently coloured speech bubble
concepts.plain: Each partner is different. Do not assume what worked with one works with another.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Professional Support
concepts.plain: If shame keeps blocking these talks, a sex therapist can help.

checks.prompt: What makes feedback about pleasure land well?
checks.explanation: Being specific, kind and timely. Giving feedback: Be specific, be kind, and be timely.

options: Not static, so the conversation continues
checks.explanation: Not static, so the conversation continues. Pleasure preferences are not static.

abb2a991-eebf-4cfb-b81a-670482cffeab.takeaway: Saying what feels good, kindly and clearly, makes sex better for everyone.
